title: Disney Parks Trivia
description: Rides, history, hidden details across Disneyland and Walt Disney World.

questions.prompt: What year did Disneyland in California open?
questions.explanation: Disneyland opened July 17, 1955 in Anaheim; the chaotic press preview day was later nicknamed 'Black Sunday' by Walt himself.

questions.prompt: What year did Walt Disney World in Florida open?
questions.explanation: Walt Disney World opened October 1, 1971 in Florida, five years after Walt's death and sixteen years after Disneyland's 1955 debut.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the iconic geodesic sphere at Epcot?
questions.explanation: Spaceship Earth is 180 feet tall and houses a slow-moving dark ride through the history of human communication, narrated over the years by Walter Cronkite, Jeremy Irons, and Dame Judi Dench.

questions.prompt: Which Disney park is in Anaheim, California?
What is the tallest mountain at any Disney park?
questions.explanation: Expedition Everest at Disney's Animal Kingdom stands 199.5 feet tall, deliberately just under 200 to avoid FAA aircraft warning light requirements.

questions.prompt: How many 'mountains' are there in Magic Kingdom at WDW?
questions.explanation: Space Mountain, Big Thunder Mountain, and Splash Mountain (now Tiana's Bayou Adventure) form the classic Magic Kingdom mountain trio.

questions.prompt: What was the original name of the ride now called Tiana's Bayou Adventure?
questions.explanation: Splash Mountain (1989-2023) was based on Song of the South; Disney rethemed it to The Princess and the Frog and reopened it in 2024.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the railroad in Magic Kingdom?
questions.explanation: The Walt Disney World Railroad circles the Magic Kingdom with four restored steam locomotives Walt's team found in Mexico in the late 1960s.

questions.prompt: Which Disney park has a castle inspired by Neuschwanstein in Bavaria?
questions.explanation: Sleeping Beauty Castle in Anaheim took visual cues from King Ludwig II's Neuschwanstein Castle and is the smallest of all Disney park castles.

questions.prompt: Which park's castle is the largest, located in Shanghai Disneyland?
questions.explanation: Opened in 2016, the Enchanted Storybook Castle is the only Disney castle to represent all the princesses rather than a single one.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the area in Disney parks dedicated to Star Wars?
questions.explanation: Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge opened in 2019 at Disneyland and Hollywood Studios, set on the planet Batuu between Episodes VIII and IX.

questions.prompt: What hidden Disney character motif is famously found throughout the parks?
questions.explanation: Hidden Mickeys are three-circle Mickey silhouettes tucked into ride details, attraction queues, and resort decor by Imagineers as a game for guests.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the central street that leads to the castle?
questions.explanation: Main Street, U.S.A. is modeled after Walt's hometown of Marceline, Missouri at the turn of the 20th century.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Tokyo Disney's second park?
questions.explanation: Tokyo DisneySea opened in 2001 and is the only Disney park built around a nautical theme; it is operated under license by the Oriental Land Company.

questions.prompt: In what city is Disneyland Paris located?
questions.explanation: Disneyland Paris is technically in Marne-la-Vallée, about 32 km east of central Paris, and opened in 1992 as Euro Disney Resort.

questions.prompt: What was the original name of EPCOT?
questions.explanation: Walt envisioned EPCOT as a real working city of the future, but after his death in 1966 the concept was reworked into a theme park that opened in 1982.

questions.prompt: Which ride features the song 'Grim Grinning Ghosts'?
questions.explanation: 'Grim Grinning Ghosts' was composed by Buddy Baker with lyrics by X. Atencio for the Haunted Mansion's 1969 opening at Disneyland.

questions.prompt: What attraction features 'It's a Small World (After All)'?
questions.explanation: The Sherman Brothers wrote the song for the 1964 New York World's Fair version of the ride, which Disney later moved to Disneyland in 1966.

questions.prompt: What year did Walt Disney die?
questions.explanation: Walt died December 15, 1966 of lung cancer at age 65, ten months before the Pirates of the Caribbean ride he was overseeing opened at Disneyland.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Disney's nighttime fireworks show often performed at Cinderella's Castle?
questions.explanation: Happily Ever After ran 2017-2021, was replaced by Disney Enchantment, then returned in 2023 as the Magic Kingdom's headline nighttime spectacular.
